question: When does the government pay for insurance losses, and after what trigger?
answer: It depends on the program, and none pays without its own trigger record. TRIP: federal share after a certified act, insurer deductible and program trigger under statute. NFIP: federal primary flood-insurance program with contractors, reinsurance and borrowing. State catastrophe fund: statutory wholesale reimbursement layer. Guaranty association: limited post-impairment or insolvency protection. PBGC: federal limited guarantee for covered private defined-benefit pensions. An FHLBank advance is a secured liquidity loan from a government-chartered member-owned bank. Program authority and available capacity are not a paid federal claim.

sections.title: The public-loss waterfall: every box
sections.sub: Government occupies different positions in different waterfalls. Compare primary insurance, wholesale reinsurance, guarantees, secured liquidity, assessments, borrowing and fiscal payment without calling every public role a bailout.

sections.title: Strategic industries: federal caps, indemnity and federal insurance
sections.sub: Strategic activity uses distinct private layers, caps, indemnities and federal insurance. Federal catastrophe regimes do not use one generic “backstop.” They combine different legal devices: mandatory private insurance or financial responsibility, exclusive or channeled liability, reciprocal waivers, liability caps, retrospective industry assessments, government-issued insurance, contractual indemnity, federal claim payment subject to appropriation, and sometimes a separate compensation system.

sections.title: Crop insurance: a federal corporation and private insurers
sections.sub: Federal crop insurance is neither wholly private insurance nor direct first-dollar federal benefits. Congress supplies authority and appropriations; FCIC, administered through RMA, establishes policy and reinsurance terms; approved private insurers sell and service policies; producers pay a subsidized premium share; and underwriting results are divided under the Standard Reinsurance Agreement.

research.title: How insurers invest trillions, move risk and share losses with government
research.answer: U.S. insurance runs through many separate regulators, very large insurer balance sheets, reinsurance and public loss programs that together work as one system. Each authority, company, contract and payment still keeps its own legal identity and timing.
